claims: A golf Grand Slam is defined as winning the Masters, PGA Championship, U.S. Open, and The Open Championship in a single calendar year.
Only Bobby Jones achieved the golf Grand Slam in 1930.
Gene Sarazen, Ben Hogan, Gary Player, Jack Nicklaus, Tiger Woods, and Rory McIlroy.
The career Grand Slam consists of winning the Masters, PGA Championship, U.S. Open, and The Open Championship over the course of a player’s career.
Rory McIlroy completed his career Grand Slam in 2025.
Rory McIlroy completed his career Grand Slam at the Masters.
Jack Nicklaus is the only player to complete the career Grand Slam multiple times.
Jack Nicklaus completed the career Grand Slam 3 times.
Jordan Spieth has three legs of the career Grand Slam and needs the PGA Championship.
Phil Mickelson has three legs of the career Grand Slam and needs the U.S. Open.
Scottie Scheffler has three legs of the career Grand Slam and needs the U.S. Open.
Tiger Woods held all four professional major titles simultaneously in 2000–2001.
Tiger Woods is the only player to hold all four professional major titles simultaneously.
In 1930, Bobby Jones won the U.S. Open, U.S. Amateur, The Open Championship, and British Amateur in one year.
The original Grand Slam consisted of the U.S. Open, U.S. Amateur, The Open Championship, and British Amateur.
The PGA Grand Slam of Golf was played from 1979 to 2014.
The PGA Grand Slam of Golf was a special tournament for that year's four major winners.
The PGA Grand Slam of Golf is distinct from the accomplishment of winning the four majors.
